We summarize the [docs](https://docs.cloudlab.us/basic-concepts.html).
It also has two tutorials, using an OpenStack cloud or Chef respectively, which we do not say here.

# Concepts

## Profiles

Performing an experiment requires specifying both the hardware resources and the software artifacts.

### Resource Specification

To do this, the [RSpec](https://docs.cloudlab.us/advanced-topics.html#%28part._rspecs%29) format is used.
Nodes can be virtual machines or physical servers, and we need to specify the amount of RAM, cores, etc.

### Software Artifacts

(Disk) images, often contains an installation of a full operating system (for booting) in addition to other software.
Alternatively, configuration can be included on a node by trasnferring during startup service hooks.

## Experiments

Profiles are instantiated into experiments that uses resources on CloudLab clusters.
Disk state of an experiment is ephemeral (which loses the data once the experiment ends).
Thus, [datasets](https://docs.cloudlab.us/advanced-storage.html) are useful.

## Control Network

While the *experiment network* is specified by the topology connecting nodes (as defined in the RSpec), the *control network* is internet accessible and so is useful on top of it.
In general, the control network should only be used for [monitoring](https://docs.cloudlab.us/advanced-topics.html#(part._introspection)), or one-time setup/termination activities.

# Resources

## Reservations

Resources can be reserved per-cluster per-type (tied to a project).
This does not start an experiment, but only ensures they are available, and are given elastically (e.g. more may be available).

## geni-lib

[geni-lib](https://docs.cloudlab.us/geni-lib/index.html) is a tool for creating resource specification (RSpec) files.
For example, to construct a profile with a single Xen VM, first we have our imports

```{python}
import geni.portal as portal
import geni.rspec.pg as rspec
```

Where the **portal context** to create **requests** for us (and the corresponding RSpec).

There are lots of default profiles, for example the [small-lan profile](https://www.cloudlab.us/show-profile.php?project=PortalProfiles&profile=small-lan).

### Virtual Machines

```{python}
request = portal.context.makeRequestRSpec()
node = request.XenVM("node")
node.cores = 2
node.ram = 2048 # 2 GB
node.disk = 8 # 8GB additional space
portal.context.printRequestRSpec()
```

Note that an alternative way of specifying additional storage is with a request for an ephemeral blockstore (aka a local dataset), e.g.

```{python}
bs = node.BlockStore("bs", "/mydata")
bs.size = "8GB"
bs.placement = "nonsysvol"
```

More details can be found at [https://docs.cloudlab.us/virtual-machines-advanced.html].

### Physical Machines

Another example, to get an ARM physical machine ([m400](zhttps://docs.cloudlab.us/hardware.html) is the hardware type for ARM) is as follows:

```{python}
request = portal.context.makeRequestRSpec()
node = request.RawPC("node")
node.hardware_type = "m400"
portal.context.printRequestRSpec()
```

These nodes can be linked within a LAN

```{python}
node1 = request.XenVM("node1")
node2 = request.XenVM("node2")
link = request.Link(members = [node1, node2])
```

The last part that we will say here (more in the docs) is to install and execute services.
A common use case is to fetch a tarball (and is installed after the disk image is loaded), before one of the scripts is executed.

```{python}
node.addService(rspec.Install(url="http://example.org/sample.tar.gz", path="/local"))
node.addService(rspec.Execute(shell="bash", command="/local/example.sh"))
```

### Switches

Configuring custom switches is also [possible](https://docs.cloudlab.us/advanced-topics.html#(part._user-controlled-switches)).

## Storage

Finally, more details about storage.

### Image-Backed Datasets

We can take a snapshot of a local dataset (see above) to a Disk Image, following [instructions](https://docs.cloudlab.us/advanced-storage.html#(part._storage-example-imdataset)).
Thus, this is a way of persisting data and using it in future experiments.

### Remote Datasets

Alternatively, we can collect it from the network, following [instructions](https://docs.cloudlab.us/advanced-storage.html#%28part._storage-example-remote-nfs%29).
